steps.text: Cold night, long night.
The bare earth is covered in frost. Upon it are haphazard footsteps, stretching into the distance where the sun fades beneath the horizon.
Scattered black dots are moving slow, at the place where the earth meets the night sky.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Lake Neva... is frozen.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: This year is bloody cold. It's not even winter yet... what are you laughing about?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I remember that in the winter of 31, Igor Velikiy defeated the army defending Grypherburg on Lake Neva, spelling the end of the Hippogryph Kingdom.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: And what about it? You want to lead us in an assault on Deity Grypherburg?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No. Not yet, at least.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Hmph... it's another story that I'm thinking of.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Around the year 150, a famous playwright wrote a play about Igor Velikiy before he entered Grypherburg.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: His intention was to celebrate the friendship between Igor and the Hippogryph noble Mikhail, who were comrades in the revolution overthrowing the Hippogryph Kingdom.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: But it was lambasted throughout Ursus because it mentioned a 'compromise' between Igor and certain Hippogryph nobles, whereby Igor gave up some power in exchange for their support.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: The Ursus refused to accept it. They considered it a slander against Igor Velikiy.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: The playwright paid the price for a story that he claimed to be true to history.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: It was only many years after his death, when the original agreement between Igor and the Hippogryph nobles was discovered, that people learned he had been telling the truth.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: A fine story.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Are you trying to tell me that the legend that I worship is just a figment of human imagination?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I'm trying to tell you that even Igor knew the importance of flexibility.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: We should stop here, Rankin.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Grypherburg is in the way, and its defenses are on a completely different level from the Far North.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: What if they find us? It won't be the Patrol Units waiting for us, but the Armies of Ursus.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Winter will find us in the wilderness if we continue to take detours and fail to reach the border in time.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I would much rather deal with a patrol or two, than Ursine winter.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Do we really have to go to the Kazimierzian border, though? Find your legendary Reunion?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: You know how far it is, never mind the enemies that we might encounter on the way. Look at our people, our food, even our clothes. Do we have enough to make it?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Let's say we actually make it to the border. What if it's not an Infected village that awaits us there, but another mine? What do we do then?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: What other way is there? Where can we go?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: There must be a way...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I know! We can go east! Nikolsk. It's an old city, almost abandoned now, and there are even fewer people in the surrounding villages.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: We could go there, split up and hide in the villages... that's the only way for us to survive.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: And live like slaves for the rest of our lives?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I gave you a choice, Nikto. I gave everyone a choice.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I thought everyone chose to come with me to live like men.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: But you shouldn't wager everyone's lives on a castle in the sky—

steps.name: Miner Scout
steps.text: I took a good look, Rankin.

steps.name: Miner Scout
steps.text: The outpost ahead is manned. The searchlights are on... it hasn't been abandoned.

steps.name: Miner Scout
steps.text: If we can't get through this way, do we have to...?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: You hear that, Rankin?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Searchlights... how many searchlights did you see?

steps.name: Miner Scout
steps.text: I... I don't really remember. Two... maybe three?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Think! How many exactly?

steps.name: Miner Scout
steps.text: Two! Yes, I remember now. There were only lights on the east and west sides. It's two lights!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Two lights... so a garrison of a hundred or so. Maybe...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Rankin!

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Look behind you, Rankin... this is all the people we have...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: This is not a revolutionary army. They just want to live.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Are you going to send them into the mines from which there is no return, like the mine owners did?
Rankin looks at the crowd behind him and sees their expressions under the lamplight.
Pain, fatigue, helplessness, fear...
Perhaps Nikto is right. Their clothes are too thin and they cannot take it. But he feels no cold, for some reason.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I won't throw away any lives. Even if sacrifice may be inevitable, I won't allow anyone to die without meaning.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We can't go back to a life of slavery...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Follow me. There's another way.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: There's such a long mine tunnel underground?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: What's going on, Rankin? How did you know where the mine tunnel was here?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Someone had an idea a few years back.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: There are more than a thousand mines in the Far North, each with hundreds of workers, yet they are all disconnected from each other. What if we changed that?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We could connect the tunnels—no one knows the underground better than we do. We could weave a web beneath the frozen soil and link everyone, sharing information and helping each other in the hour of need.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Have you been preparing all these years? Were you planning for this day?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I'm no prophet. I simply began with a very basic idea—we should unite and help each other.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: At the beginning, my influence extended only to a dozen mines in the area. I was powerless beyond that.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Later, I heard that other people were doing the same things in other places... it's a pleasant surprise to find that this tunnel looks relatively safe.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Where does it lead?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The Volgrad Mining District, southeast of Grypherburg, in the southernmost part of Ursus. If we can reach it through the tunnels, we'll be able to circumvent the capital's defenses.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: But you better pray there's no army on our tail, or it'll be an easy opportunity to wipe us out all at once.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No such thing as a path without risk.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Wait... I smell alcohol.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Impossible. How could there be—

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Get down!
A flash of cold light lunges out from the darkness, breaking the only lit lamp.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: What the—

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Get down! Don't move, and don't fire back!

steps.name: Voice From the Tunnel
steps.text: Blyat! They found us!

steps.name: Voice From the Tunnel
steps.text: Call for help!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Wait! Stop! We're friends!
Rankin stands and shouts at the top of his lungs, his voice echoing in the deepest reaches of the cavern.

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: You're not the Patrol Units?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: That's what we were about to ask... I suppose the answer is no.

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: Thank goodness! I thought they found our position.

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: Where did you come from?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The Central Mining District.

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: Central? I didn't know there were any survivors there!

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: We heard the guards started a massacre. We thought there wasn't anybody left alive.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I can see why there would be such rumors...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But they're not true. We're still alive. We defeated the Patrol Units and escaped. We haven't given up on our struggle.

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: That's the best news I've heard in a while!

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: One moment.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: We're trying to get to the Volgrad Mining District, in the south, through these tunnels. Can we—

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: The south? It's no good. The tunnel leading to the south has collapsed. That's why we've been stuck here.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Again, Rankin! Again! Why is every path a dead end?

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: Wait... Rankin? THE Rankin?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: My name's Rankin. I don't know anything about 'The' Rankin.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: It's really you! Rankin from Central! You're real—you're alive!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I see my name has taken flight on its own...

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: We can talk about that later! Let me take you to the living area.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: You folks look like you're in real bad shape. We have some food and water, not a lot, but we can spare some.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Living area? Are there a lot of you living here?

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: A lot.
They follow the lone light of the lamp and walk into the tunnel. Gradually, they begin to see the light at the end, and hear the faint sound of talking.
They go around a corner to see a large number of people—there must be hundreds of them—living in a tiny space.
Some are wearing miner's outfits, others simple cotton clothes. There are elderly, and there are children... with simple living tools around them.
This is where they live.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Worried Miner
steps.text: What's going on? Didn't you guys go on patrol? Why did you bring so many people back? Who are they?

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Friends! Let me introduce this man here—Rankin!

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Rankin! He's Rankin!

steps.name: Curious Miner
steps.text: I've heard the name before! You were the one who had the idea of linking all the mining districts!

steps.name: Hunched Old Man
steps.text: You're not as tall as the stories say, but I guess you're tall enough...

steps.name: Young Child
steps.text: Did you fight the Kazimierzians? Do the Firewatch really exist?

They rush forward to see the figure of legend. There is reverence, there is joy, and there is a little bit of disappointment in seeing the real man behind the myth, but all culminate in an excited call for his name.
Rankin, Rankin.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Alright, that's enough. Our friends have run into some trouble and they need rest.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Get some bread from the storage room, Zoya. The big loaves.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: ...Why are you living here?

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: That's a long story...

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: The Neva Dam burst three years ago, flooding the nearby mines. The overseer refused to let us come out from underground, fearing that we might flee to a nearby city.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: The mine eventually collapsed, splitting it in half. Half of us were drowned. We were the lucky half.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: We thought all we could do was wait for death, until we found a passage below that led to another mine.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: We got some food from there, but we didn't dare go above ground, so we stayed underground...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: And you've been living here? How?

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: We helped deliver cargo for other mines. Some kind-hearted people shared food with us. Sometimes we stole from the Patrol Units... just like musbeasts, eh.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: We continued to expand the passages, to the Ural in the east and Kras in the west, linking up a lot of mines and districts.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: We've taken in refugees who fled the other mines. We've got maybe a thousand people who are somewhat fit to move.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: There are children here...

steps.name: Worried Mother
steps.text: Yes... she's two years-old, and she's never seen the sun...

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: Blyat!

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: No matter what, we're still alive! All thanks to you, Rankin!

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: We'd have been long dead if you didn't come up with your idea!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No... I did nothing. Don't thank me. You found your path of life on your own.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But it shouldn't have been like this. This shouldn't have been your life.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: But... what could we do, Rankin?

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Of course we don't want to live in this hole forever, but where else can we go?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: ...Come with me.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Where to?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: South.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: To the Kazimierzian border. We'll find the village that belongs to the Infected, land that we can live on.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We'll go together.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Calm down, Rankin.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Did you forget about the Lake Neva Outpost? Did you think you could sneak past them with so many people?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Then we'll take it by force.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: You're out of your mind—

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I know what I'm talking about, Nikto!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I'm confident.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The Lake Neva Outpost will have at most a hundred men, and no heavy weapons.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Three hundred. Give me three hundred pairs of hands that can hold a crossbow and a hoe, and we'll take the Lake Neva Outpost before they have a chance to send a distress signal.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: By the time the regular supply delivery arrives weeks later, we'll be long gone, on the vast Barton Plains!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We'll only be one step away from the goal. Nothing can stop us.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: No... you've gone mad.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I don't understand... why do you always force yourself into the riskiest option? Why do you—
Rankin ignores his objections and extends his hand to the crowd.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: I see your vision, Rankin, and I'm willing to go with you to take the outpost.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: But I can't make the others follow you. They'll have to decide their own fates.
The miner shakes Rankin's hand and goes to stand behind him.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: All who are willing to go with Rankin to take the outpost, come forward.
Feet shuffle in the crowd, and several youths take their place behind Rankin.
Others remain hesitant, or find their own family hanging onto their shirts.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: Whatever the others say, I'm with you, Rankin.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: I don't know what that place for the Infected on the Kazimierzian border is like, but it can't be worse than here.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: We trust you because you're Rankin. You're the hero that united us. No matter what end awaits us—
Rankin halts those words by raising a hand. He looks down, takes a deep breath, then looks up again at the crowd, his eyes resolute.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Have you ever seen spring in Ursus?
Silence.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I have, when I was a soldier with the border guard.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: When the snow melts, green grass grows from the soil again, and the migratory fowlbeasts come back.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Sometimes, the sun is out all day, so bright it almost drives you mad, and you can only sleep by pulling your blanket over your head.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The sun, the grass, the fowlbeasts, the wind... none of those exist in the mines.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But it's not because we don't deserve it!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It's not too much to ask. These are things that you and I, your children, all of us, deserve as human beings!
Rankin's words echo in the dark mine, and in the hearts of all who are listening.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It will be dangerous. I won't lie to you, nor will I force anyone to join us.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But sacrifices are a part of any struggle. There will always be those who fall by the wayside, or leave of their own accord.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Whether they fell or left on their own, whether they were brave or timid, remember those who are around you, and remember that you once stood together and shared the same pain.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We will always be comrades.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Some may fall tonight, and some may live. Those who live will pave the path to tomorrow for the rest.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We shall raise a torch upon the outpost to remember the fallen, that survivors may remember, and the oppressor will see.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Before we leave, I want to tell you how I feel.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I hope you will join me and contribute your strength.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Only by taking this step can we go back to the surface, bathe in the sunlight, and become human again!
Rankin's chest rises and falls. He feels hot blood flow through his veins, and his strength return to him, and he raises his arms as he speaks.
More and more people come over to him, as they did when he first made his rallying cry in the mine shafts of the Central Mining District.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Brothers, sisters, remember the inhuman lives that we once led.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We were herded into the mines like beckbeasts, using our lives to dig for Originium to warm the bed of others. This is not the law; it is murder.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Yes, murder. They tried to shut our mouths, keep us captive until we die, stop us from thinking and make us numb, until we are no different from animals.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But we did not forget how to struggle. Deep underground, we connected the mines, and broke through our prison of death.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But that's not enough. We can't just keep running away. We must face our foe head-on.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Someone might ask, 'What do we do, Rankin?'

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It's difficult, but it is also easy. The first thing to do is take the first step.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Tonight's battle will be the first step. More people will learn who we are, and all those who are oppressed like we are will know that they're not alone!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Do not fear. There's no need to fear. Those who are high above are not strong. We are strong!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We have nothing to lose except our lives... if they won't give us our right, then we'll fight for it with our lives!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Ask me. Ask me, 'What do we do?' 'What will become of us?'

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: History has shown us time and again that it doesn't forgive oppressors. If punishment has not yet come, it's only because it still needs time, and anger that will set everything on fire.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Igor Velikiy ripped the wings off the high-and-mighty Hippogryphs. If his descendants are doing the same things the Hippogryphs once did, then we will drag them down from their thrones!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Our weapons will once again force Deity Grypherburg's golden gates open. Our pickaxes will dig a hole in this land, and tear its ugly, greedy face to pieces!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: All of Ursus will see us, fear us, recognize us.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Then, we will have a bright future.
